**Objectives of the Tutorial/Lab**
By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

- Derive conditional distributions for bivariate normal models.
- Implement the Gibbs sampler.
- Assess the effect of the proposal step size on the performance of the MH algorithm.
- Evaluate the performance of MH using Markov chain outputs: checking autocorrelation, effective sample size, convergence, acceptance rates.

## Question 2

**Metropolis-Hastings** [**We already solved problems (a), (b), and (c) in the week 10. This week, solve the problem (d), (e), and (f).**]

Recall that $\mathbf{X} = \begin{pmatrix} X_1 \\  X_2 \end{pmatrix} \sim N(\boldsymbol\mu, \boldsymbol\Sigma)$, with $\boldsymbol\mu = \begin{pmatrix} \mu_1 \\ \mu_2 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma^2_1 & \sigma_{12} \\ \sigma_{12} & \sigma^2_2 \end{pmatrix}$, if and only if $\mathbf{X}$ has joint density
$$
f_{\boldsymbol\mu, \boldsymbol\Sigma}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac 1{2\pi|\boldsymbol\Sigma|^{1/2}} \exp\left( -\frac{1}{2} (\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu)^T \boldsymbol\Sigma^{-1} (\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu) \right),
$$
where $\mathbf{x} = \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{pmatrix}$.
